items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: And George Washington Carver has a beautiful energy, the students have a beautiful energy in spite of how little they’ve been given to work with...

ctx.x: What would you say to people who take the attitude why are people living there and why should we as a government pay to make it possible for them to live in the same place again?

Well I mean there’s a lot of things you would say. I mean for one thing it’s the government’s fault that the flooding happened to begin with. It was the failure of the federal levies that caused the flooding. Yes, there was a hurricane involved. And there was some wind damage. But the flooding happened because of breaches in the federal levy system. Not just one or two breaches but double digits. I mean there were places where the levies were compromised because they hadn’t been built correctly to begin with. And…

might have moved back to New Orleans to help rebuild their own city. I mean there’s all sorts of things and dynamics of it that are not hard to understand, but at the same time it’s disconcerting to realize that our country, for all the greatness of our resources, on two fronts has not embraced our own culture as something that’s kind of collectively ours to share and be proud of.
